summary.notes: Anchored to OA siblings (Henthorn 2018, Li 2014, Forster 2019) because target Friedland 2010 RR1965 paper is paywalled (BioOne, no PMC, no preprint). Cannot test paper's specific 4-scenario parameter table or per-dose numerical tables.

checks.claim: Stochastic NHEJ reproduces biphasic (fast+slow) DSB rejoining curve
checks.anchor: Rothkamm & Lobrich PNAS 2003 / Karlsson & Stenerlow IJRB 2004
checks.condition: residual_5min < 0.5 AND residual_60min > 1.5 * residual_240min AND residual_24h > 0.1%

checks.claim: Residual DSB fraction at 24 h consistent with OA Henthorn 2018 (~7.3%)
checks.anchor: Henthorn 2018 Sci Rep 8:2654 (~7.3% at 24h, largely LET-independent)

checks.claim: Dirty (complex) DSBs are the source of the slow rejoining component
checks.anchor: Abstract: 'three of four scenarios overestimate residual DSBs ... dirty-end processing is the multi-step slow contribution'

checks.claim: Under tight-geometry (R_syn=25nm, D=1e-4 um^2/min), the slow tail is dominated by failed synapsis, NOT by dirty-end processing
checks.note: In the tight-geometry regime, dirty-end content does not affect long-time residual. This shows the structural replication's behavior is sensitive to the synapsis geometry parameters, which are exactly the parameters that the paper's 4 scenarios presumably vary - and which are inaccessible behind the paywall.

checks.claim: Mis-rejoin fraction increases with dose (proximity-driven misrepair)
checks.anchor: Abstract; Forster 2019 HNSCC alpha_mr=0.02 Gy^-1, beta_mr=0.37 Gy^-2 (super-linear)

checks.claim: At least one model scenario badly overestimates residual DSBs after low-dose IR
